name: Critical minerals
summary: China's rare-earth export-control pause expires 10 Nov with no renewal announced
state: China's one-year suspension of its October 2025 rare-earth export controls expires on 10 Nov, and no formal renewal had been published as of 6 Nov (Mining Technology; Motley Fool). Lapsed controls would bring back tighter licensing. No production stoppages outside China have been confirmed, so the Alert line is not crossed.
for_you: Makers of magnets, cars, electronics and defence equipment are most exposed if licensing tightens again. Consumers are unlikely to see shortages immediately.
rubric_hit: Watch: export controls due to return 10 Nov; no confirmed stoppages outside China

sources.title: Mining Technology — China rare earth export pause nears expiry amid persistent supply concentration
Motley Fool — China's rare-earth export pause expires Nov. 10

why: Rare earths, gallium, germanium and graphite are chokepoints for chips, EVs and defence — and China dominates processing.
drivers: Export controls, trade disputes, mine outages, stockpiling.

rubric.alert: Export bans in force that are causing reported production stoppages outside China.
rubric.watch: New export controls announced or licensing slowed.
rubric.normal: No new export restrictions in the past month.
